title: Potion Shop Calculator
body:
Goal: write three functions that return answers, and a docstring.

  1. Open starter.py in Thonny.
  2. TODO 1: total_cost() returns price times quantity.
  3. TODO 2: can_afford() returns True or False.
  4. TODO 3: write a docstring for coins_left(): one sentence in triple quotes that says what it does.
  5. TODO 4: finish coins_left(). Tip: you can call can_afford() inside it!
  6. Run it. Try buying 3 potions, then 5.

Done looks like: buying 3 potions costs 36 coins and leaves 14. Buying 5 costs 60 coins: too expensive, so you keep all 50.

Extra: add a discount(cost) function: if the cost is 40 or more, return the cost minus 5.

hints.label: Hint 1
hints.title: Where to look
hints.html: Each function has pass right now, so it hands back nothing. Read each docstring and TODO to see what each function should give back. Run the shop with 3 potions and see what it prints.

hints.label: Hint 2
hints.title: Try this
hints.html: Use return to hand back an answer. Multiply with *. A comparison like >= gives True or False. A docstring is a sentence in triple quotes right under the def line. A function can call another function.

hints.label: Hint 3
hints.title: Almost there
hints.html: Write return ____ * ____ and return coins >= ____. For coins_left, put your docstring first. Then use if can_afford(____, ____): to choose between two return lines. The TODO tells you what each one gives back.

    pass


def coins_left(coins, cost):
    # TODO 3: write a docstring on the line above this one, like the others.
    # TODO 4: if you can afford it, return coins - cost. Otherwise return coins.
    pass


if __name__ == "__main__":
    coins = 50
    price = 12
    print(f"You have {coins} coins. Potions cost {price} coins each.")
    how_many = int(input("How many potions do you want? "))
    cost = total_cost(price, how_many)
    if can_afford(coins, cost):
        print(f"That costs {cost} coins. Here you go!")
    else:
        print(f"That costs {cost} coins. Sorry, you cannot afford it.")
    print(f"Coins left: {coins_left(coins, cost)}")
